[MUQATIL:79:34-41/r7] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The transgressor is fixed in shirk, chooses worldly life over the next, does not fear God or judgment, and consumes what is forbidden; Hell is his abode.
[FARRA:v3p232/r10] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | The Fire is the abode of the people just characterized in the passage.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | reports | Some take the article al- as replacing the possessive pronoun, so al-maʾwā means “his refuge”; the vocative command “lower the gaze, man” likewise means “your gaze,” as in the poet’s line.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p281/r3] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · الشاعر | reports | The poet’s “lower the gaze” addresses a man whose gaze is meant; this supports reading al-maʾwā as “his refuge” for both Hell and Paradise.
[NAHHAS:v5p146/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الكوفيون | reports | Kufans parse fa-hiya maʾwāhu, with alif replacing a pronoun; Basrans parse hiya al-maʾwā lahu.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Al-maʾwā is the place that shelters or receives him.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says Hell is the abode of whoever has this description.
[JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Choosing worldly life over the Hereafter is blameworthy, whereas choosing the Hereafter is praiseworthy.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#3/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The response after فإذا is ‘then the matter is as follows’; الجحيم هي المأوى means Hell is his abode, with a known possessor understood rather than expressed, and هي is either a separator or subject.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | المأوى is the dwelling where someone settles and remains.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Hell is the abode for the transgressor.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#5/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj treats this as the answer to the clause if the Overwhelming Event comes.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r10] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The phrase may elide له after al-maʾwā because the meaning is clear, as in the command lower your gaze; Rāzī also reads it as the fitting abode for such a person.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r9] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Rāzī infers that the sinner who lacks these two defining traits is not described as having Hell for his permanent abode.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After describing Resurrection generally, God divides those morally responsible into wretched and blessed, beginning with the wretched.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The Fire is the person's refuge; the definite article in al-maʾwā stands in place of the possessive pronoun.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Hell is the tyrant’s refuge; the definite article substitutes for a possessive, and هي may be a separator or subject.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The Fire is the place of return.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | He contrasts this with the abode of the one who fears his Lord's standing and restrains his soul from desire. | mentions 79:40, 79:41
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · الكوفيين | reports | The Kufans take the definite article as a substitute for a possessive construction.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#17/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · سيبويه والبصريين | reports | Sibawayh and the Basrans understand it as “the place of refuge for him.”
[QASHANI:79:34-41/r4] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Transgressors exceed human nature’s balance toward animal or predatory ranks and prefer sensory pleasure to real life, so hell becomes their home.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Basran grammar supplies an omitted pronoun, المأوى له; the Kufans treat ال as replacing it. Al-Zamakhshari gives فإن الجحيم مأواه, but Abu Hayyan finds no subject-predicate link in his analysis.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الكوفيون | reports | The phrase may mean هي المأوى له, or مأواه with أل substituting for the possessive pronoun; the latter is the Kufan position.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | One of those analyses must supply the predicate's link back to the subject; omitting an overt link is eased by the phrase's position at a verse ending.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A cited poem combines أل with a possessive pronoun, which would be unexpected if أل replaced that pronoun; the author uses it against the Kufan account.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari glosses it as the transgressor's abode, comparing it to غض الطرف: possession is understood, not replaced by أل, and both things are definite by context.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The Shaykh objects that al-Zamakhshari supplies no link to the subject: he rejects the Kufan view and does not posit the pronoun that Basrans posit.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:39/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author answers that al-Zamakhshari's appeal to what is understood is exactly the Basran analysis, and questions how the Shaykh missed this.
[BURHAN:v4p334/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · الكوفيون | reports | The Kufans supply the omitted complement as ‘it is his refuge.’
[BURHAN:v4p334/r10] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | When a predicate precedes inna, the lām can attach to the fronted phrase; the underlying order is ‘they wander in their intoxication.’
[BURHAN:v4p334/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · البصريون | reports | The Basrans supply the omitted complement as ‘it is the refuge for him.’
[BURHAN:v4p334/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The article’s lām is normally light; in the name Allah it is emphatic after a preceding fatḥa or ḍamma, conveying reverence for God.
[BURHAN:v4p334/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The lām in demonstrative names signals distance or reinforces it; grammarians differ on which function it has.
[BURHAN:v4p334/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | With weakened inna, the lām is called the initial or differentiating lām because it distinguishes the affirmative particle from negative inna and confirms the predicate. | mentions 69:12, 90:17, 47:21
[BURHAN:v4p334/r6] BURHAN, d. 794 · الكوفيون | reports | The Kufans take lām to mean ‘except’ in affirmative clauses, with inna meaning ‘not’; al-Kisa’i reads the verb with the nominative on this basis.
[BURHAN:v4p334/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisa’i reads ‘to make the mountains disappear’ in the nominative and understands the clause as ‘their plot was only intended to make them disappear.’
[BURHAN:v4p334/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Emphatic lām can precede a subject or occur with inna on a delayed subject or predicate; inna emphasizes what follows and lām emphasizes the predicate.
[BURHAN:v4p334/r9] BURHAN, d. 794 · سعيد | reports | Sa‘id reads the hamza of inna open in ‘they surely eat’; the author explains that its lām is licensed only with kasra-inna or with a fronted predicate.
[BURHAN:v4p37/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The definite article can stand in for a pronoun: Hell is its refuge for the one who preferred worldly life, while Paradise is the refuge for the one who feared God.
[BURHAN:v4p37/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · الكوفيون | reports | The Kufans explain the definite article in these refuge phrases as a substitute for the omitted pronoun.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · البصريون | reports | The Basran grammatical analysis supplies an omitted pronoun after hiya in the phrase meaning that Hell is the abode for the transgressor.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الكوفيون | reports | The Kufan analysis makes the definite article al stand in for the omitted pronoun, an analysis Abū Ḥayyān attributes to them.
[BURSEVI:v10p254/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Hell is the unbelieving transgressor’s permanent abode; believers who sin may leave it, so the passage addresses disbelievers while warning other readers.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The Kufans treat the article in al-maʾwā as replacing the possessor’s pronoun, yielding ‘his refuge’; Basrans instead understand ‘the refuge for him.’ The omitted possessor is obvious, and the ending suits the rhyme.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#3/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Alusi says هي is either a separative pronoun or a subject referring to Hell; the clause then restricts refuge to Hell alone. Al-Zamakhsharī chooses the latter explanation of the omitted possessor.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو حيان | reports | Abū Ḥayyān prefers taking the response to إذا as the clause beginning فأما; Alusi considers this sound and says the syntax is straightforward if the preceding clause is conditional. | mentions 2:38
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Alternatively, the response to إذا is omitted and the تفصيل clause explains it; other suggestions derive the omission from what precedes or follows, which Alusi finds unconvincing.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The blame concerns choosing worldly life over the afterlife; worldly benefits that do not cost one the afterlife are not blameworthy, as the counsel to Qarun shows. | mentions 28:77
[TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.

[TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The two classes are unbelieving wrongdoers and faithful, pious people; the fate of the weak and those mixing good and bad deeds is left to God, who may forgive or accept intercession.

[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | These brief verses summarize negative and positive attitudes that prepare either immense loss or salvation in the afterlife.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Verse 39 reminds these people of their bad end.
